subject: Management-plane connectivity drift and emergency rollback briefing
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@medcarecloud.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: medcarecloud-ops@medcarecloud.com, James Park <james.park@medcarecloud.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Intermittent management-plane connectivity from our VPC

Hi Kimberly —

We started seeing spikes in control-plane errors at ~08:45 PT and by 09:00 our customer-facing services began timing out on model fetches. The SDK retries are masking some errors but our throughput dropped ~40%.

Attached are the short logs we pulled (agent-logs-20261202.tar.gz) and a clip of the kube events (k8s-events-output.txt). Can you confirm if any Redwood-side upgrade or config change happened this morning?

We’re happy to hop on a quick bridge — this is impacting two production clusters.

Thanks,
Anita
SRE Lead, MedCare Cloud

attachments: agent-logs-20261202.tar.gz (archive, 2.1MB), k8s-events-output.txt (text, 35KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@medcarecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, medcarecloud-ops@medcarecloud.com
Date: 2026-12-02T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Intermittent management-plane connectivity from our VPC

Anita — thanks for the quick heads up and the logs. We are not performing a platform-wide upgrade in the hosted fleet right now; however there was a staged rollout to the private controlplane agent that began at 08:30 PT (customer opt-in).

Initial triage notes:
- I’ve seen repeated TLS handshake resets between the controlplane and agent in the logs you attached.
- A subset of agents are showing a reconnect storm when the agent attempts eviction/reconnect during leader re-election.
- Marcus/Dylan—can you confirm whether the rollout contained the recent connection backoff change?

Immediate next steps:
1) We will put the rollout on hold for all customers.
2) Marcus will propose a rollback plan within 30 minutes.
3) I’ll schedule a 30-minute bridge with your ops and our oncall for 09:45 PT — if that time doesn't work, tell me and I’ll adjust.

I’ve uploaded a provisional rollback runbook and the incident link to our incident tracker: https://redwood-incidents.example.com/INC-20261202-MGMT-DRIFT

—Kimberly
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---
attachments: runbook-privatenet-rollback.pdf (pdf, 220KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Management-plane connectivity — rollout details

Quick confirmation: the private agent rollout did include the connection backoff tuning (change-set ID: cs-20261130-connbackoff). It was intended to reduce noisy reconnects, but the telemetry shows an interaction with customers using older kube-proxy versions that causes reconnection thrashing when leader election timers overlap.

Rollback plan (high level):
- Target: pause agent rotation and revert to cs-20261120 baseline for controlplane agent.
- Scope: MedCare Cloud clusters tagged with privatennet:mcare (we have a host list).
- Impact: anticipated 10–15m controlplane interruption per agent during revert; plan to stagger across AZs.
- Rollback runbook reference: https://drive.google.com/privatenet-runbook-rollback (uploaded by Kimberly).

I’ll draft the stagger schedule and post to the incident tracker; Dylan will coordinate the bridge.

—Marcus
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@medcarecloud.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: medcarecloud-ops@medcarecloud.com
Date: 2026-12-02T09:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Management-plane connectivity drift and emergency rollback briefing

Hi Anita / MedCare team —

Thanks for joining the bridge earlier. Recap and immediate mitigation we executed at 09:50 PT:
- We paused the rollout across all private agent cohorts.
- Began orchestrated rollback to cs-20261120 on a single AZ in your staging cluster; rollback completed for that AZ at ~10:05 PT and we observed a ~65% reduction in error rates for the affected control-plane calls.
- Staggered rollout of rollback to remaining AZs is in progress; expected completion by 11:15 PT.

Requested from MedCare: can you confirm whether any custom network policies or packet-inspection appliances are performing TLS interception? There are a few TLS anomalies in the logs that suggest middlebox rewrites.

Next follow-ups:
- I will post per-AZ completion times to the incident tracker.
- Marcus to run a full candidate verification before we unpause the next agent rollout.

If you want us to hold the rollback at any point, reply with "HOLD" and we will pause.

—Dylan
Oncall, Runtime Reliability

Date: 2026-12-02T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Management-plane connectivity drift and rollback briefing — update from our side

Thanks team — rollback progress looks good. A couple of notes from our SREs after AZ-B completed at 11:05 PT:
- They confirmed an IPS appliance in front of the cluster is doing occasional TLS re-negotiation for inspection; it seems to correlate with the timestamps where agent handshakes failed.
- No internal config changes on our side this morning.

Two asks:
1) After your rollback completes, can Redwood provide a short postmortem that includes root cause, the decision criteria for rollback, and a timeline of when the cs-20261130 variant can be reintroduced safely?
2) We would like the postmortem to include an explicit list of mitigation steps we can apply on our side (e.g., MTLS client cert pinning guidance, recommended kube-proxy versions).

Appreciate the speed on this. We’ll keep monitoring.

—Anita
SRE Lead, MedCare Cloud
